summary: cache-index-mismatch triggers cold KV lookups on repeated prompts causing timeouts
description: Issue summary: BrightWrite Labs reports repeat prompts (identical user messages sent sequentially) are experiencing significantly higher latencies and occasional 504 timeouts starting 2026-03-12 08:30 UTC. Impact: production traffic for a dedicated tenant; customer reports degraded UX with repeat prompt cases in their chat product, estimated 18% of requests hitting the slow path for recent hour. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated-nyc-1), prod, us-east-1 region. Observed: p50 increased from ~60ms to ~320ms, p95 from ~220ms to ~1.8s for repeat prompts; error spikes of 504/timeouts at ~0.6% during peak. Immediate customer impact: user-facing failures and latency spikes for repeated-turn interactions (e.g., quick clarifications).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightWrite workload profile (short prompts, many repeated messages). 2) Send a sequence of identical prompts (same token prefix and length distribution) at moderate concurrency (~30 qps). 3) Observe tail latency and occasional 504 responses after 2000-3000 requests. 4) Compare behavior after forcing cache warm vs cold. Note: issue reproduces consistently when a background shard rebalance/eviction occurs.
logs:
Selected logs (us-east-1 serving node IDs): 
- 2026-03-12T08:29:57Z node-07 serving-runtime: INFO request id=rx-9f3 dropped to cold-path; missing prefix-index entry for prompt_hash=0x7a2b
- 2026-03-12T08:30:02Z kv-cache: WARN prefix-index-mismatch during lookup, fallback to full-index-scan (duration=420ms)
- 2026-03-12T08:30:05Z api-gateway: ERROR upstream timed out 504 for request rx-9f3 after 2000ms
- 2026-03-12T08:31:12Z scheduler: INFO shard-rebalance triggered; evicted prefix-mapping entries count=8421
Metrics: p95_tokens_per_request +1.6s correlated with prefix-index-scan counts rising by 12x.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: recent shard rebalancer change (rollout-2026-03-11) evicts prefix-index metadata too aggressively; when a repeat prompt arrives after eviction the runtime falls back to a slow code path that does a full index scan to rebuild prefix->kv mapping, causing large per-request latency. Evidence: correlating rebalance events with spike windows, logs show 'prefix-index-mismatch' and subsequent 'full-index-scan' durations ~300-500ms. Reproduction: running a synthetic workload that toggles a small eviction window reproduces increased p95 and occasional upstream timeouts. Temporary mitigation: raise prefix retention TTL and stop the aggressive rebalance on affected shard set — this reduced 504s to near zero for BrightWrite test cluster. Related to PR referenced above that adjusted rebalance eviction thresholds. Next: create a targeted fix to ensure fallback path uses an async rebuild that doesn't block request path, add circuit-breaker to stream fallback, and add monitoring alert on index-scan rate.
comments: Support (Emily): Customer reported degradation at 08:30 UTC after overnight traffic increase. Collected traces and initial logs, escalated to SRE.
SRE (Mateo): Confirmed correlation between scheduler rebalance and latency spikes. Created reproduction against dedicated-nyc-1. Temporary mitigation applied (raise retention TTL on shard set).
Customer (BrightWrite PE): Confirmed immediate improvement after mitigation. They still want a permanent guarantee to avoid regressions during rebalances.

Eng (Priya Rao - runtime): Looking into fallback path. Suspect synchronous index rebuild on request path is the primary contributor. Proposing async warm/rebuild + rate-limiting for rebuilds. Will open a patch.
resolution: Mitigation applied: increased prefix-index retention TTL for BrightWrite's dedicated shard set and paused automatic rebalance rollout in us-east-1. Long-term fix: engineering to land changes that make prefix index rebuild asynchronous and non-blocking (PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1847). Follow-ups: add alerting for 'full-index-scan' rate > 50/min, add canary tests for rebalance behavior, and schedule postmortem with action items (owner: Mateo, due 2026-03-20).
follow_up_actions: ENG-1794: make prefix-index rebuild async and rate-limited
OPS-2120: add alert for full-index-scan spike
CS-412: notify BrightWrite when fix is scheduled for prod rollout
